ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The A gene of Arabidopsis thaliana is located on chromosome 1 and affects the frequency of chromosome crossing over during meiosis; the a gene does not have this function. The B gene is located on chromosome 5 and causes the four pollen grains from the same pollen mother cell to separate; the b gene does not have this function. Plant Jia (AaBB) and plant Yi (AAbb) are used as parents to carry out a crossing experiment, and the required plant Bing (aabb) is obtained in F2. The a gene was obtained by inserting T﹣DNA into the A gene. When using the PCR method to determine the insertion position of T﹣DNA, which two primer combinations should be selected from Figure 1?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The A gene of Arabidopsis thaliana is located on chromosome 1 and affects the frequency of chromosome crossing over during meiosis; the a gene does not have this function. The B gene is located on chromosome 5 and causes the four pollen grains from the same pollen mother cell to separate; the b gene does not have this function. Plant Jia (AaBB) and plant Yi (AAbb) are used as parents to carry out a crossing experiment, and the required plant Bing (aabb) is obtained in F2. The a gene was obtained by inserting T﹣DNA into the A gene. When using the PCR method to determine the insertion position of T﹣DNA, which two primer combinations should be selected from Figure 1?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 1, the T-DNA fragment is inserted in the middle of the A gene fragment, and A gene fragments are still marked on the left and right sides of the inserted fragment respectively. Primers Ⅰ, Ⅱ, and Ⅲ are marked in the figure, among which primer Ⅱ is located near the right end of the T-DNA fragment, and primer Ⅲ is located in the right-side A gene fragment. Their directions face each other, so they can amplify across the junction region between T-DNA and the right-side A gene fragment. Reasoning: The a gene is formed after T-DNA is inserted into the A gene. To use PCR to determine the insertion position of T-DNA, one primer located on T-DNA and one primer located on the flanking sequence of the A gene should be selected, and the extension directions of the two primers should face each other, so that a fragment spanning the insertion boundary can be amplified. In the figure, primers Ⅱ and Ⅲ meet this requirement.
